appraisal_events.evidence: un oncle de Swann... mourut, laissant toute cette fortune à Gilberte qui devenait ainsi une des plus riches héritières de France... Forcheville... déclara qu'il l'adoptait.
appraisal_events.explanation: An enormous inheritance and Forcheville's formal adoption transform Gilberte into one of the wealthiest heiresses in France, bearing an aristocratic name in place of her father's.

appraisal_events.evidence: cet absurde nom de Swann gênerait le mariage. Il déclara qu'il l'adoptait ... un antisémitisme mondain s'en trouvait au contraire accru et exaspéré.
appraisal_events.explanation: Amid a resurgence of fashionable antisemitism after the Dreyfus affair, Swann's name is treated by Forcheville as an embarrassment to be erased even from his own daughter, posthumously discrediting Swann through the social stigma attached to his name.

appraisal_events.evidence: Mme de Guermantes... s'était... refusée à recevoir sa fille aussi bien que sa femme. Ce refus avait été en apparence d'autant plus cruel que ce qu'avait pendant longtemps représenté à Swann son mariage possible avec Odette, c'était la présentation de sa fille à Mme de Guermantes.
appraisal_events.explanation: The duchess pointedly and lastingly refuses to receive Swann's wife and daughter after his marriage, permanently closing off the one social door he had most wanted opened.

appraisal_events.evidence: elle lui avait raconté comme une chose très drôle et extraordinaire que je l'avais suivie et frôlée, la prenant pour une cocotte.
appraisal_events.explanation: Gilberte recounts to the duchess, as an amusing anecdote, that the narrator had once followed and brushed against her in the street, mistaking her for a kept woman, turning his earlier blunder into circulated social comedy at his expense.

status_effects.explanation: Sudden wealth and formal adoption into the Forcheville name visibly raise her standing, making her one of the richest heiresses in France.
His own name is treated, even posthumously, as a liability to be erased from his daughter's identity because of resurgent social antisemitism.
He is durably barred, along with his wife and daughter, from the duchess's circle, closing off the social presentation he had most desired.
His earlier mistake in the street is retold as a droll story at his expense, mildly diminishing him in the retelling even as it is treated lightly.

ambiguities: The duchess's old refusal (E3) named both Swann's wife and daughter, but Gilberte is shown in this same passage now welcomed and at ease in the duchess's salon; her present standing is read as elevated (E1) rather than carrying forward that earlier exclusion.
